title: How Google Beam connects military families globally
gist: Google and the USO are bringing HP Dimension with Google Beam, a 3D video communication system, to 20 USO locations worldwide so deployed service members can connect with families. A docuseries follows four soldiers from the 2nd Battalion, 37th Armored Regiment, and the pilot is expanding from Poland and Fort Bliss to Germany and Fort Hood.

insights.claim: Google is partnering with the USO to bring HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 USO locations globally so deployed service members can bridge distance from their families.
insights.speaker: Josh Woodward
insights.so_what: This is a deployment of about 20 sites. It is a visible real-world use of Beam, and the article gives no revenue or sales figures.
insights.quote: we’re partnering with the USO to bring HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 USO locations globally
insights.locator: For deployed service members, the hardest distance

insights.claim: The Beam pilot started earlier this year connecting families between Trzebień, Poland and Fort Bliss, Texas, and is now expanding to Grafenwöhr, Germany and Fort Hood, Texas.
insights.speaker: Josh Woodward
insights.so_what: The staged rollout from a pilot to more bases points to a phased expansion.
insights.quote: Google Beam began a pilot program connecting families between Trzebień, Poland, and Fort Bliss, Texas earlier this year.
insights.locator: Google Beam began a pilot program

insights.claim: Google pitches Beam as a true-to-life 3D video experience in which families feel they are stepping into the same room, which it says phone calls cannot do because they lack body language and eye contact.
insights.speaker: Josh Woodward
insights.so_what: The product is positioned as a premium alternative to ordinary video calls, with an emotional use case as its marketing.
insights.quote: Beam’s unique true-to-life, 3D video communication experience, families feel like they’re stepping into the same room
insights.locator: That's why we’re partnering with the USO

themes.theme: Docuseries as emotional proof of product value

insights.claim: The docuseries was directed by veteran filmmaker Kyle Hausmann-Stokes and follows four soldiers from the 2nd Battalion, 37th Armored Regiment (Iron Dukes) deployed in Poland as they connect with families at home.
insights.speaker: Josh Woodward
insights.so_what: Google is marketing Beam through storytelling rather than through technical specs.
insights.locator: Directed by military veteran and filmmaker

insights.claim: The four featured families cope with problems such as an eight-hour time difference that makes milestones like a promotion hard to share, long deployments (one chaplain has been deployed 15 months in his first two years), and standard phone calls that make it hard to bond with a newborn and a toddler.
insights.speaker: Josh Woodward
insights.so_what: These use cases (milestones, young children, time zones) show where Beam is meant to beat voice and flat video calls.

insights.claim: Army Chaplain Roland Kassales says that conveying feeling and body language in communication will go a long way toward soldiers' overall well-being.
insights.speaker: Roland Kassales
insights.so_what: A user testimonial links the technology to well-being outcomes, which is an anecdotal claim and not a measured one.
insights.quote: Being able to incorporate feeling and body language — all those things that make communication meaningful — will go a long way towards overall well-being for soldiers.
